<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Sp1nd01" /></noinclude>from the hope of the Goſpel, which yee haue heard, {{smaller|and}} which was preached to euery creature which vnder heauen, whereof I Paul am made a Miniſter.

{{Verse|1|24}} Who now reioyce in my ſufferings for you, and fill vp that which is behind of the affictions of Chriſt in my fleſh, for his bodies ſake, which is the Church,

{{Verse|1|25}} Whereof I am made a Miniſter, according to the diſpenſation of God, which is giuen to mee for you, ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, fully to preach the word of God, Rom.''1.19.}} to fulfill the word of God:

{{Verse|1|26}} {{smaller|Euen}} the myſtery which hath been hid from ages, and from generations, but now is made manifeſt to his ſaints,

{{Verse|1|27}} To whom God would make knowen what is the riches of the glory of this myſterie among the Gentiles, which is Chriſt ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, amongst you.''}} in you, the hope of glory:

{{Verse|1|28}} Whom we preach, warning euery man, and teaching euery man in all wiſedome, that we may preſent euery man perfect in Chriſt Ieſus.

{{Verse|1|29}} Whereunto I alſo labour, ſtriuing according to his working, which worketh in me mightily.

==={{Chapter|2|CHAP. II.}}===
{{smaller block|[[#2:1|1]] Hee ſtill exhorteth them to bee conſtant in Chriſt, [[#2:8|8]] To beware of Philoſophie, and vaine traditions, [[#2:18|18]] worſhipping of Angels, [[#2:20|20]] and Legall Ceremonies, which are ended in Chriſt.}}

{{Verse|2|1|notext=}}{{dropinitial|F|image=King James Bible (1611) page A2r (F).png|imgsize=100px}}Or I would that ye knew what great ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, feare or care.''}} conflict I haue for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as haue not ſeene my face in the fleſh:

{{Verse|2|2}} That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in loue, and vnto all riches of full aſſurance of vnderſtanding, to the acknowledgement of the myſterie of God, and of the Father, and of Chriſt,

{{Verse|2|3}} ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, wherein.''}} In whom are hid all the treaſures of wiſedome, and knowledge.

{{Verse|2|4}} And this I ſay, left any man ſhould beguile you with entiſing words.

{{Verse|2|5}} For though I bee abſent in the fleſh, yet am I with you in the ſpirit, ioying and beholding your order, and the ſtedfaſtneſſe of your faith in Chriſt.

{{Verse|2|6}} As yee haue therefore receiued Chriſt Ieſus the Lord, {{smaller|so}} walke yee in him:

{{Verse|2|7}} Rooted and built vp in him, and ſtabliſhed in the faith, as yee haue bene taught, abounding therein with thankeſgiuing.

{{Verse|2|8}} Beware leſt any man ſpoile you through Philoſophie and vaine deceit, after the tradition of men, after the ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, elements''}} rudiments of the world, and not after Chriſt:

{{Verse|2|9}} For in him dwelleth all the fulneſſe of the Godhead bodily.

{{Verse|2|10}} And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principalitie, ⁊ power.

{{Verse|2|11}} In whom alſo ye are circumciſed with the Circumciſion made without handes, in putting off the body of the ſinnes of the fleſh, by the Circumciſion of Chriſt:

{{Verse|2|12}} Buried with him in Baptiſme, wherein alſo you are riſen with {{smaller|him}} through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raiſed him from the dead.

{{Verse|2|13}} And you being dead in your ſinnes, and the vncircumciſion of your fleſh, hath hee quickened together with him, hauing forgiuen you all treſpaſſes, 

{{Verse|2|14}} Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances, that was againſt vs, which was contrary to vs, and tooke it out of the way, nayling it to his Croſſe:

{{Verse|2|15}} And hauing ſpoyled principalities and powers, he made a ſhew of them openly, triumphing ouer them ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, in himſelfe.''}} in it. 

{{Verse|2|16}} Let no man therefore iudge you in ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, for eating and drinking.''}} meat, or in drinke, or in ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, in part.''}} reſpect of an Holy day, or of the New moone, or of the Sabbath {{smaller|dayes:}}

{{Verse|2|17}} Which are a ſhadow of things to come, but the body {{smaller|is}} of Chriſt.

{{Verse|2|18}} Let no man ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, iudge againſt you.''}} beguile you of your reward, †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Gr. being a voluntary in humilitie.''}} in a voluntary humilitie, and worſhipping of Angels, intruding into thoſe things which hee hath not ſeene, vainely puft vp by his fleſhly minde:

{{Verse|2|19}} And not holding the head, from which all the body ioynts and bands hauing nouriſhment miniſtred, and knit together, increaſeth with the increaſe of God.

{{Verse|2|20}} Wherefore if yee be dead with Chriſt frō the ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, elements.''}} rudiments of the world: why, as though liuing in the world, are ye ſubiect to ordinances?

{{Verse|2|21}} (Touch not, taſte not, handle not:

{{Verse|2|22}} Which all are to periſh with the vſing) after the commandements and doctrines of men:

{{Verse|2|23}} Which things haue in deed a ſhew<noinclude></noinclude>
